name: Apache DataFusion
workload: ClickBench (43 queries, 100M-row hits table, Parquet single-file) run head-to-head on the same AWS instance type as part of ClickHouse's public ClickBench suite.
claimed_speedup: ~1.6x faster than DuckDB on ClickBench total query time on c7a.metal-48xl (DataFusion 9.78s vs DuckDB 15.70s, sum of best-of-3 per query) (derived from page data)
hardware: AWS c7a.metal-48xl (AMD EPYC 9R14, 192 vCPU) - ClickBench standard hardware; CPU model implied by instance type, not stated verbatim on the results page
tradeoffs: Rust ecosystem, not a drop-in SQL client for existing DuckDB/ClickHouse users; embeddable query engine rather than a full DBMS; result run dates for DataFusion (2026-08-20) and DuckDB (2026-05-11) are not the same day, so versions differ slightly.
caveats: Comparison is derived by us from two separate rows of ClickBench's public results file, not a single page stating '1.6x'; ClickBench does not publish per-engine compiler flags (both likely official release builds), so this is capped at tier B; on other machine sizes/dates the gap narrows or reverses for some queries (not verified per-query).
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): ClickHouse/ClickBench data.generated.js, cross-referenced after query 'ClickBench db-benchmark h2oai results fastest'

name: Databend
workload: ClickBench (43 queries, 100M-row hits table) run head-to-head on the same AWS instance type as part of ClickHouse's public ClickBench suite.
claimed_speedup: ~1.6x faster than DuckDB on ClickBench total query time on c7a.metal-48xl (Databend 9.91s vs DuckDB 15.70s, sum of best-of-3 per query) (derived from page data)
hardware: AWS c7a.metal-48xl (AMD EPYC 9R14, 192 vCPU) - ClickBench standard hardware
tradeoffs: Core engine is Apache-2.0 but enterprise/EE binaries (ee_main.rs paths) are under the Elastic-2.0 license, so a full build mixes licenses; separately, Databend's own marketing benchmark (docs.databend.com/guides/benchmark/tpch, Databend Cloud vs Snowflake, SF100) shows only ~1.1-1.25x on hot/cold query time despite a '3x faster' headline claim - treat the headline figure skeptically.
caveats: ClickBench run dates differ (Databend 2026-09-26 vs DuckDB 2026-05-11); no compiler/flags published for either engine on the results page, capping tier at B; the separate Databend-vs-Snowflake TPC-H claim compares baseline_in_list=false (Snowflake) and is materially weaker (~1.1-1.25x) than the '3x' marketing headline, so we report the DuckDB/ClickBench figure instead as the more defensible claim.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): ClickHouse/ClickBench data.generated.js

name: QuestDB
workload: Streaming 500 million rows of trades data (symbol, side, price, amount, timestamp) out of the database into Apache Arrow format over the network, using a public reproducible harness, comparing QuestDB's new QWP protocol against ClickHouse's native and Arrow-over-HTTP egress paths.
claimed_speedup: 1.55x faster than ClickHouse's fastest configuration of any kind (QuestDB 220M rows/s vs ClickHouse 142M rows/s), 2.35x faster than ClickHouse's fastest streaming-to-Arrow configuration (vs 94M rows/s)
hardware: AWS m8gn.8xlarge (32 vCPU, 123GB RAM, 100Gbps) server, c8gn.8xlarge (32 vCPU, 61GB RAM, 100Gbps) client
tradeoffs: Result is specific to result-set egress/streaming into Arrow, not general query execution speed; QuestDB is JVM-based (GC pauses, JIT warm-up) vs ClickHouse's native C++; benchmark measures a narrow protocol (QWP) QuestDB just introduced, so it is inherently favorable framing.
caveats: First-party QuestDB blog post; harness is public and reproducible (github.com/javier/questdb_qwp_egress_to_arrow_perf) but QuestDB/ClickHouse versions and compiler flags are not stated, so per the rules this is capped at C ('project's own benchmark code with partial methodology'), not B. QuestDB also beats DuckDB on ClickBench itself (5.40s vs 15.70s on c7a.metal-48xl, tier B, derived from page data) as corroborating but separate evidence.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): questdb.com/blog listing, cross-checked against ClickHouse/ClickBench data.generated.js

name: Umbra
workload: ClickBench (43 queries, 100M-row hits table) run as part of ClickHouse's public independent ClickBench suite.
claimed_speedup: ~11.8x faster than DuckDB and ~2.5x faster than ClickHouse on ClickBench total query time on c7a.metal-48xl (Umbra 1.33s vs DuckDB 15.70s vs ClickHouse 3.29s, sum of best-of-3 per query) (derived from page data)
hardware: AWS c7a.metal-48xl (AMD EPYC 9R14, 192 vCPU) - ClickBench standard hardware
tradeoffs: Umbra is a TUM research prototype (Neumann et al.) with no public source release; its commercialized descendant is the closed-source CedarDB. The idea (compiling queries with fused execution, morsel-driven parallelism) can be studied from published papers but the code itself cannot be obtained or copied.
caveats: No public repository, so evidence_tier is capped at B per the rules (peer-reviewed/well-known independent suite showing the win, code not available). Only usable as a reference/'research' entry; smaller instance sizes in the same ClickBench dataset show more errors for Umbra (4-14 failed queries), so the win margin at c7a.metal-48xl should not be assumed universal.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): ClickHouse/ClickBench data.generated.js

name: data.table (R)
workload: h2oai db-benchmark groupby task 'sum v1 by id1' on a 100M-row, 100-group synthetic table (G1_1e8_1e2_0_0), on a 244GB RAM / 32-core r3-8xlarge EC2 instance.
claimed_speedup: ~2.8x faster than pandas (data.table 1.14.1: ~0.88-1.17s vs pandas 1.2.4: ~2.73-2.88s, best-of-run timings) (derived from page data: h2oai.github.io/db-benchmark/time.csv)
hardware: r3-8xlarge EC2 (244GB RAM, 32 cores), per the benchmark README
tradeoffs: R, not C++/Python-native (though internals are C); pandas also failed to complete the 1e9-row (1B row) groupby tasks in this suite at all (out of memory) while data.table, polars, and pydatatable completed them, a bigger practical gap than the raw timing ratio suggests at the largest scale.
caveats: The h2oai/db-benchmark repo itself has not been updated since 2023-06-29 (>3 years, effectively abandoned) and its last actual timing run was 2021-01-20, using pandas 1.2.4, data.table 1.14.1, and polars 0.7.16 - all now many major versions behind current releases, so the margin vs current pandas is unverified and likely narrower given pandas 2.x improvements.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): starting query 'ClickBench db-benchmark h2oai results fastest' -> h2oai.github.io/db-benchmark/time.csv

name: SlothDB
workload: Author-run comparison of SlothDB against a user-supplied DuckDB binary using bench/clickbench (the 43 ClickBench queries verbatim) and a custom bench/run.py harness, plus an earlier HN claim citing a 14GB/100M-row hits.parquet ClickBench-style comparison against DuckDB and ClickHouse.
claimed_speedup: Originally announced as 1.35x-5x faster than DuckDB and ClickHouse (HN, 2026-05-01); the project's own current README explicitly walks this back, calling README/bench numbers 'anecdotal, not from standardised benchmark hardware' and noting wins are 'query-shape-specific' due to a per-query handler-dispatch path rather than the general engine
hardware: Not stated (author says 'one workstation', no CPU model given)
tradeoffs: Early-stage/experimental per the author; no vendor PR to the real ClickBench is open; the project itself says some benchmark wins come from special-cased per-query handlers rather than the general query engine, which is a materially weaker and more overfit claim than a general engine speedup.
caveats: Self-disclosed low-confidence result: the maintainer explicitly warns readers not to treat the numbers as final and flags that they are not from standardized hardware and may reflect query-specific handler dispatch rather than a real architectural win over DuckDB/ClickHouse. Included per the 'tag instead of exclude' rule, but confidence is set low.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia query 'faster than DuckDB' -> 'SlothDB a 5X Faster Alternative to DuckDB, ClickHouse DB' (2026-05-01)
